newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. signs quake insurance agency measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. signs quake insurance agency measure.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson signed controversial legislation on Friday to create a $10.5 billion publicly-run agency to sell earthquake insurance to homeowners.
Wilson, a Republican, said the legislation should help to end California's insurance availability crisis for homeowners seeking earthquake coverage.
"Earthquakes will always be a fact of life in California, but homeowners no longer must risk a devastating, unrecoverable loss because they couldn't get insurance," Wilson said.
The legislation signed Friday will implement the so-called California Earthquake Authority. The proposal was approved by the Legislature in August after months of heated debate.
California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said the authority should begin to sell policies by December 1.

"Gov. Wilson's signature on legislation creating the California Earthquake Authority means that California's economic recovery will proceed on course -- uninterrupted by the evaporation of homeowners' insurance and the paralyzing effect that would have on the state's real estate market," Quackenbush said in a statement.
As a public entity, the authority will be tax-exempt, enabling it to build up enough reserves to cover major earthquake disasters.
The authority will be capable of funding $10.5 billion through a combination of sources, including insurer contributions, policyholder premiums, capital markets, and reinsurance.

Quackenbush maintains that the authority would, in its first year of operation, have enough resources to pay all claims from an earthquake more than twice as destructive as the devastating 1994 Northridge quake.
Wilson said mammoth natural disasters like the Northridge quake create a magnitude of loss that can plunge an insurance company into insolvency.
Such disasters, coupled with California's requirement that homeowner policyholders be offered earthquake insurance, have severely restricted the availability of these policies.

The California Department of Insurance estimated that about 99 percent of California insurers had restricted or stopped selling homeowner and earthquake insurance, making it difficult for homebuyers to obtain mortgages.
"The CEA (California Earthquake Authority) will provide much-needed relief for the insurance availablility shortage," Wilson said.
